claims.claim: Born in Venice, parish of San Bartolomeo, probably 1484, per Menegazzo's research on official documents
Competing birth years 1484, 1467 or 1464; English Wikipedia gives Padua as birthplace and calls him the son of an innkeeper who claimed a connection to the noble Cornaro family
Padua civic museums give his dates as 1480/84 to 1566
Father Antonio di Giacomo; family name possibly originally Righi; claimed descent from Doge Marco Corner; 1514 petition for patrician recognition rejected after four years
Mother Angeliera Angelieri
Sent to Padua in 1489 to his maternal uncle Alvise Angelieri; inherited nearly the whole estate on Angelieri's death in 1511
Married Veronica Agugia in 1517; only child Chiara married Giovanni Corner on July 1, 1537

September 13, 1529 contract with Cardinal Francesco Pisani to administer the lands of the bishopric of Padua; 1530 partnership to drain about 1,600 campi; November 23, 1541 order to destroy the dikes after Cristoforo Sabbadino's opposition
Giovanni Maria Falconetto, a Veronese architect, designed the buildings; the Loggia was completed in 1524; donated to the city of Padua in 1968
Loggia built in 1524 as a fixed theatrical backdrop; Odeo a place for music and intellectual pastimes
Odeo dated about 1530; Ruzzante performed his comedies in the Loggia before his patron Alvise Cornaro
Ruzzante became manager of Alvise Cornaro's farm in 1529; died March 17, 1542
Ruzzante lived in the guest quarters of Cornaro's house in Padua
Della vita sobria published 1558, followed by three further writings in 1561, 1563 and 1565
Illness between his thirty-fifth and fortieth year; daily allowance of twelve ounces of food and fourteen ounces of wine
Trattato dell'architettura deals with private dwellings; he also wrote a Trattato di acque
Died May 8, 1566, in Padua; buried in the Basilica del Santo
Older English edition says he died at Padua on April 26, 1566, being above an hundred years old
He claimed to be 56 in 1540, 70 in 1551, 80 in 1557, 85 in 1559 and 95 in 1565
Wikipedia reports ages at death of 98 or 102 depending on the source, and that he deliberately overstated his age
Portrait by Tintoretto, about 1560 to 1565, Galleria Palatina, Florence

quotes.text: It is a thing past all doubt, that custom, by time, becomes a second nature
quotes.source: A Treatise on a Sober Life, opening sentence (English translation of the 1558 discourse)

quotes.text: I never knew, till I grew old, that the world was beautiful.
quotes.source: Discourses on a Sober and Temperate Life (English translation)

uncertain: Birth year: 1484 (Treccani, following Menegazzo, from his official declarations), about 1480 (Padua museums give 1480/84), 1467 and 1464 (older tradition, listed by Wikipedia). The profile uses probably 1484.
Birthplace: Treccani and Italian Wikipedia say Venice (parish of San Bartolomeo); English Wikipedia says Padua.
Age at death: about 82 if born in 1484; 98 or 102 in older sources; the Gutenberg edition says above an hundred. His own stated ages are inconsistent and inflated (Treccani).
Death date: May 8, 1566 (Treccani, Wikipedia) against April 26, 1566 (older English edition on Project Gutenberg).

Noble status: his claim of descent from Doge Marco Corner was his own; the 1514 petition was rejected (Treccani). The older English edition repeats his version that the family was deprived of nobility by relatives' misconduct. Father as innkeeper appears only in English Wikipedia.
Dates of the later discourses: Treccani gives 1561, 1563, 1565; English Wikipedia gives writing dates of 1553, 1558 and 1562 and a collected edition of 1583 to 1595. The profile follows Treccani.
Trattato di acque: Treccani dates it 1560, Wikipedia (English and Italian) 1566. Year omitted from the profile.
Odeo date: about 1530 (Padua museums); Treccani says presumably contemporary with the Loggia begun in 1524; Italian Wikipedia says begun 1524.
Diet quantities: the Gutenberg English translation says twelve ounces of food and fourteen of wine; Italian Wikipedia says 20 ounces of wine; English Wikipedia converts to 350 g and 414 mL.

The quotes are from an English translation whose translator and original print date were not confirmed in a fetched page, so the translation year is omitted. Chiara's eleven children and the exact year of English first translation were not included.
